title: A study to assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, immunogenicity and antitumour activity of IPN60300 in adults with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumours
official: An Open-Label, Phase I/II First-in-Human, Dose Escalation, Dose Optimisation and Dose Expansion Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetic, Pharmacodynamic, Immunogenicity and Antitumour Activity of IPN60300 as Single Agent in Adult Participants with Locally Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumours.
summary:
Main objective: Phase Ia
To evaluate the safety and tolerability of IPN60300 as a single agent and determine the MTD/MAD in participants with tumour type of interest 
Phase Ib
To determine the optimal dosing regimen ofIPN60300 in participants with selected tumour(s)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. (1) Participant must be ≥18 years of age, at the time of signing the informed consent.
2. (10) At the time of screening, a tumour tissue specimen is required for enrolment into the dose escalation and dose optimisation portions of the study for retrospective central laboratory determination
3. (11) Capable of giving signed informed consent which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form (ICF)
4. (12) Have a life expectancy of more than 3 months for disease-related mortality, as evaluated by the investigator
5. (2) Participants with histologically or cytologically documented, locally advanced, or metastatic solid tumours that relapsed or were refractory after being previously treated with standard of care therapy; or for which there is no available established therapy; or standard therapy is contraindicated or not deemed appropriate by the treating investigator.
6. (3) Participants must have measurable disease per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (RECIST) version 1.1.
7. (4) Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 to 1.
8. (5) Male and female participants: Contraceptive use by men or women should be consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies.
9. (6) Adequate bone marrow function within 7 days before first dose of study intervention
10. (7) Adequate renal function within 7 days before first dose of study intervention
11. (8) Adequate hepatic function or laboratory abnormalities indicating hepatic injury within 7 days before first dose of study intervention
12. (9) Prothrombin time or international normalised ratio (INR) ≤1.5 × ULN
Exclusion criteria:
1. (1) Known second malignancy either progressing or requiring active treatment within the last 2 years prior to first dose of study intervention within the last 2 years prior to first dose of study intervention.
2. (10) History of noninfectious interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis/radiation pneumonitis that required steroids or has current ILD/pneumonitis.
3. (11) Clinically significant gastrointestinal disorder including bleeding, occlusion, diarrhoea >Grade 1, malabsorption syndrome, ulcerative colitis, inflammatory bowel disease or partial bowel obstruction.
4. (12) Any evidence of severe active infection or inflammatory condition
5. (13) Significant concurrent, uncontrolled medical condition that would put participants at unacceptable risk from study participation or preclude them from complying with study procedures as per investigator assessment
6. (14) Participants with uncontrolled human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). HIV-infected participants are eligible if they meet the criteria described in protocol
7. (15) Known active infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) OR hepatitis C virus (HCV). Participants are eligible if they meet the criteria described in protocol
8. (16) Prior anticancer therapy, including chemotherapy, targeted therapy, therapeutic anticancer antibodies, or radio-/toxin-immunoconjugates
9. (17) Ongoing immunosuppressive therapy, including systemic corticosteroids.
10. (2) Residual toxicity from prior anticancer therapy that are NCI CTCAE version 5.0 Grade 2 or higher. Stable chronic Grade 2 toxicities from previous treatments may be eligible per the judgement of investigator.
11. (3) History of major surgery within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study intervention
12. (4) Previous solid organ transplantation
13. (5) Pre-existing, acute or chronic severe corneal disorders, sequelae from severe cornedisorders, or a history of corneal transplantation
14. (6) Active brain metastases or leptomeningeal metastases with exception to asymptomatic and treated brain metastases
15. (7) History of stroke or significant cerebrovascular disease (ie, transient ischemic attack) within 6 months prior to initiation of study intervention.
16. (8) History of clinically significant cardiac disease within 6 months prior to the initiation of study intervention, including but not limited to unstable angina, acute myocardial infarction, endoscopic or open-heart cardiac surgery, or heart failure classified as NYHA Grade 2 or higher
17. (9) History of clinically significant respiratory disease within 6 months prior to the initiation of study intervention, including severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or asthma.
